snippet.title: 15 Steps You Must Take Immediately After an EMP Attack (Before It's Too Late)
snippet.description:

snippet.title: Winter is Coming - Is the Texas Grid Ready?
snippet.description:
Secretary of Energy Chris Wright breaks down the critical relationship between peak electricity demand and grid design, focusing on winter reliability challenges. Wright discusses how extreme weather events create peak demand scenarios when renewable sources may not be available.

Texas figured this out the hard way during Winter Storm Uri where 246 people died due to lack of heat when the grid failed. 

🎯 Key Topics Covered:
Peak electricity demand during winter weather events
Grid reliability during high-pressure weather systems
The role of dispatchable vs. non-dispatchable power sources
Analysis of renewable energy availability during peak demand
Reference to recent Texas winter storm Uri power outages

⚡ About Peak Demand:
Wright explains that electrical grids must be designed for peak demand scenarios - typically cold winter evenings when heating needs are highest and renewable generation may be limited due to weather conditions.

📊 Data Point Mentioned:
Inauguration Day renewable energy contribution: 2-3% from wind, solar, and batteries during peak demand

🔥 Why This Matters:
Understanding grid reliability is crucial for energy policy discussions and infrastructure planning. Wright emphasizes the importance of dispatchable power sources for maintaining grid stability during critical periods.

snippet.description:

We ranked all 50 states using five questions built on public data: can the grid borrow power, where its fuel comes from, its outage record, the weather it faces, and how dangerous a week without power would be there. And number one is not Texas.

How to Survive an Earthquake in the Philippines (Complete Guide)

The Philippines experiences over 150 earthquakes per year, and experts warn "The Big One" could strike Metro Manila at any time. Your survival depends on preparation and knowing exactly what to do before, during, and after an earthquake.

This complete guide covers everything Filipino families need to know to survive an earthquake.

🚨 REMEMBER: DROP, COVER, HOLD ON

DROP to hands and knees
COVER under sturdy furniture
HOLD ON until shaking stops

PHIVOLCS warns a magnitude 7.2+ earthquake on the Valley Fault System could cause:
- 34,000 deaths
- 100,000+ injuries
- 340,000 destroyed homes
- ₱2+ trillion in economic losses

The time to prepare is NOW.
